title: New York Times Cooking Is Now Available on AI Glasses from Meta
summary: New York Times Cooking is now available on AI glasses from Meta, giving home cooks with the glasses a new way to follow trusted recipes while keeping their hands on the task in front of them.
body_markdown:
A new hands-free cooking experience for AI glasses from Meta users brings audio instructions, voice commands, and glanceable recipe steps to the kitchen.


New York Times Cooking is now available on[AI glasses from Meta](https://www.meta.com/ai-glasses/) , giving home cooks with the glasses a new way to follow trusted recipes while keeping their hands on the task in front of them.


Home cooks can pair compatible glasses with the[NYT Cooking iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/nyt-cooking-quick-tasty-meals/id911422904) to follow recipes hands-free, hearing each step and navigating by voice. On compatible Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses, steps also appear in the lens, with gesture navigation available through the Meta Neural Band. Learn more about supported glasses and how to get[started](https://help.nytimes.com/3924077) .


The experience launches with about 3,000[recipes available](https://cooking.nytimes.com/68861692-nyt-cooking/13395693-our-50-most-popular-recipes-of-all-time-so-far) for hands-free cooking, with more planned over the next year.


Recipes are easy to follow by ear, with ingredient amounts included where cooks need them. Instructions are read aloud using The Times’s existing text-to-speech technology. Cooks can say “next” or “back” to move between steps, “repeat” to hear a step again, or ask for help with navigation. They can always see their place in the original recipe in the NYT Cooking app.


Hands-free is a new way to interact with our expert recipes and does not create new recipes. This feature was designed in line with The New York Times Company’s[privacy](https://help.nytimes.com/10940941449492-The-New-York-Times-Company-Privacy-Policy) policy; the feature never accesses the glasses’ camera and does not share users’ NYT Cooking interactions with Meta.


Hands-free cooking builds on Cooking’s investment in practical tools in the app, including Cook Mode and Recipe Customization, that help users discover, modify and cook recipes successfully. Together, these experiences bring Cooking’s trusted recipes and expertise to home cooks in more useful ways, helping them feel more confident in the kitchen.
